slice: Two-stroke engines: porting, power valves, port timing, and how to change the power - KTM/Husqvarna/GasGas TBI 125/150/250/300 (2023-2026, plus carbureted 2020-2022 125/150/250 SX and TC/MC) and Yamaha YZ125/YZ250 (2020-2026)

records.statement: The 250 TBI two-stroke has a 66.4 mm bore and 72 mm stroke for 249 cc.

source.name: Motocross Action - First look 2023 KTM fuel-injected two-strokes

records.notes: KTM spec as reproduced by MXA; same figures in Dirt Bike, Ultimate Motorcycling and MCNews. Carbureted 2020-2022 250 SX/TC250 share 66.4 x 72.

records.statement: The 300 SX is the 250 SX with a bigger cylinder and piston: 72 mm bore x 72 mm stroke for 293.2 cc, on the 250's bottom end.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2024 KTM 250/300SX

records.notes: MXA states the 300SX shares the 250SX bottom end; Twisted Development test also says the two differ only in cylinder and piston.

records.statement: The 125 TBI two-stroke has a 54 mm bore and 54.5 mm stroke for 124.8 cc.

source.name: Motocross Action - First look 2023 KTM fuel-injected two-strokes

records.notes: Also 54 x 54.5 on carbureted 2020-2022 125 SX/TC125.

records.statement: The carbureted 150 SX uses a 58 mm bore on the 125's 54.5 mm stroke for 143.9 cc, fed by a 38 mm Mikuni carburetor, kick start only.

source.name: Motorcycle.com - 2022 KTM SX 150 specifications

records.notes: Ultimate Motorcycling reports the 150 SX was dropped for MY2023 when the TBI range arrived.

records.statement: The 2020-2022 KTM/Husqvarna SX/TC two-strokes used a 38 mm Mikuni TMX carburetor, which the 2023 throttle body replaced.

source.name: MCNews - 2023 KTM SX two-strokes

records.notes: MXA 2020 YZ125 vs 125SX test notes the 2020 YZ125 and KTM 125SX used the same carburetor.

records.statement: From 2023 the SX/TC two-strokes use a 39 mm Keihin throttle body with two injectors, one before and one after the throttle butterfly. This is not transfer-port injection.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2023 KTM 300SX

records.notes: Dual-injector placement from MXA 2023 300SX and 2024 125SX tests. Premix ratios from MXA first look. GasGas MC models adopt the platform from MY2024 per VHM application tables.

records.statement: From 2024 the XC-W enduro two-strokes moved from TPI to a 39 mm Keihin throttle body with two staged injectors, oil injection, a new plastic-flap reed case and an electronically controlled, self-calibrating power valve.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2024 KTM XC-W lineup first look

records.notes: Article lists 150 XC-W stroke as 54 mm; the SX 150 stroke is 54.5 mm, likely rounding. Off-road models are outside the MX focus but share cylinder architecture.

records.statement: The TBI bikes replaced the centrifugal ball-ramp power valve with an electric-motor, gear-driven valve that the ECU opens according to rpm and throttle position.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2023 KTM 300SX

records.notes: Dirt Bike first look describes the replaced system as a centrifugal ball-ramp mechanism; Dirt Bike TC250 test says exhaust port timing now depends on rpm and throttle opening.

records.topic: map switch effect on power valve (250/300)
records.statement: On the 250/300 TBI, map 1 (white) only lets the power valve open about 80%, which mutes power; map 2 (green) opens it fully.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2023 KTM 300SX

records.notes: Reported by MXA in 2023 300SX and 2024 250/300SX tests (not a published KTM spec). On MXA's dyno the 300SX maps were identical to 6,700 rpm, then map 2 pulled ahead: 55.0 vs 54.19 hp peak.

records.statement: On the 125 TBI the two maps change fuel and ignition only; the power valve is not used to separate the maps. The green map is a rich 'safety' map that MXA testers found bogged randomly.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2024 KTM 125SX

records.notes: MXA report; KTM does not publish map contents.

records.statement: The 250/300 TBI engines have a 'torque chamber' at the exhaust port that is opened at low rpm and closed at high rpm, adding volume to the exhaust at low speed.

values.behaviour: open at low rpm, closed at high rpm

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2024 KTM 250/300SX

records.notes: Volume and switching rpm not published. Two Stroke Performance sells a larger power-valve cover claimed to add low-rpm torque (3,000-5,000 rpm) by increasing this chamber volume.

records.statement: For 2023 KTM rotated the two-stroke engines rearward by 2 degrees and fitted new cylinder heads; KTM claims under 24 kg for the 300 engine and under 18 kg for the 125 engine.

source.name: Motocross Action - First look 2023 KTM fuel-injected two-strokes

records.notes: Weights from MCNews; KTM's 2026 250 SX page gives 23.9 kg engine weight.

records.statement: KTM claimed more than 57 hp for the 300 SX at launch.

source.name: MCNews - 2023 KTM SX two-strokes

records.notes: Manufacturer claim, measurement basis not stated; magazine rear-wheel dynos read 48.8-55.0 hp (see conflicts).

records.topic: power valve calibration after top-end work
records.statement: The electronic power valve must be re-taught its end stops after the cylinder is removed: plug in the brand's wake-up dongle with throttle held at half for 10 seconds, then release so the valve cycles. Skipping it can make the bike bog or not rev.

source.name: ADB Magazine - How to reset a KTM TBI power valve

records.notes: Procedure as described by ADB from dealer practice; each brand (KTM/Husqvarna/GasGas) uses its own dongle.

records.statement: Owners report the electronic power valve can stick and wear as hours build, with an occasional metal burr in the first valve-shaft hole.

source.name: Vital MX - Feedback on new fuel-injected KTM two-strokes?

records.notes: Single unnamed forum post; treat as an early-warning sign to inspect, not a known failure rate.

records.statement: The carbureted KTM 250 power valve starts opening at about 5,600 rpm with stock preload and is fully open at about 7,900 rpm with the stock yellow inner spring. Each full turn of the preload screw moves the opening point about 150 rpm.

source.name: Motocross Action - This much we know: making the most of the power valve on your KTM 250/300

records.notes: MXA figures; ADB Magazine gives identical numbers. Article covers KTM 250SX/300 (carbureted, pre-2023); mechanical design shared by Husqvarna and GasGas 250s. Likely the same figures are reprinted from KTM's own guidance.

records.topic: power valve preload screw - direction and feel
records.statement: Turning the preload screw clockwise (in) gives smoother power and broader bottom end; counterclockwise (out) gives more hit and maximum top end. Adjust in 1/8 turns; total range is six turns.

source.name: Motocross Action - Ask the MXperts: fine-tuning the KTM 250SX two-stroke

records.notes: CONFLICT on direction: MXA 'This much we know' and ADB say one turn out opens the valve 150 rpm sooner (smoother) and in opens later (more hit), the opposite of MXA's Ask the MXperts text. See conflicts. Do not loosen the two screws holding the brass adjuster body.

records.statement: Three colour-coded inner springs set how fast the valve opens and where it is fully open: yellow is stock, red snaps it open quicker (more aggressive), green opens it slower (softer).

source.name: Motocross Action - Ask the MXperts: fine-tuning the KTM 250SX two-stroke

records.notes: No spring rates published. MXA testers usually stay on yellow.

records.topic: power valve main spring wire size
records.statement: Owners report the stock primary power-valve spring is 2.0 mm wire on the 125/150/250/300; a 1.8 mm wire spring (KTM part 54637072000) is used to open the valve earlier for more midrange.

source.name: Vital MX - 2015 SX250/TC250 suggested mods

records.notes: Forum posts by 15tc150 and Husky_250 (2019). Not verified against KTM parts data.

records.statement: On carbureted SX models a white connector near the fuel tank selects the ignition map: unplugged is the soft map, plugged together is the stock performance map. Some models have a handlebar switch (1 mellow, 2 aggressive).

source.name: Motocross Action - This much we know: making the most of the power valve on your KTM 250/300

records.notes: Husqvarna TC250 handlebar switches reportedly work on the KTM.

records.statement: The Kreft PowerDial replaces the preload screw with a hand dial; MXA's starting point was fully counterclockwise then 1.5 turns clockwise, adjusting in quarter turns. MXA called half-turn changes very noticeable.

source.name: Motocross Action - Team tested Kreft PowerDial power valve adjuster

records.notes: Only for mechanical (carbureted-era) power valves; TBI bikes have no preload screw.

records.topic: 150 SX power valve settings used by owners
records.statement: Owners of the 150 SX report running the stock yellow spring with the preload screw 1.75 to 2.5 turns in from fully out; one moved from 5 turns in to 2 turns in and found it much better but still narrow.

source.name: Vital MX - 2019 KTM 150SX questions

records.notes: Forum reports, 2020.

records.statement: Rotating the stator: retarding 1-2 degrees smooths the hit and lengthens the pull, advancing sharpens throttle; owners warn never to go beyond 3 degrees either way.

source.name: Vital MX - 2015 SX250/TC250 suggested mods

records.notes: Forum post (15tc150, 2019); three 8 mm bolts move the stator plate.

records.statement: Stock TBI mapping is conservative and runs flat into the rev limiter; a Twisted Development remap kept the easy bottom end, added throttle response and mid-to-top pull, and reduced limiter hits. Pipe-specific maps exist (FMF, Pro Circuit, DR.D).

source.name: Motocross Action - Team tested Twisted Development KTM 250/300 remapped ECU

records.notes: No dyno numbers published. Keefer (2023 300SX) described stock as rich and lethargic and the remap as adding low-rpm response and 2nd/3rd gear pull. Tuners such as WMR and Jamie Ellis cracked the locked ECU.

records.statement: Two Stroke Performance's handheld ECU Reflash Module switches between stock and a TSP map and can change fuel, ignition, oil delivery and power-valve settings; claimed smoother curve and less pipe bang, no dyno data.

source.name: Slavens Racing blog - TSP parts for TBI KTM two-strokes (Brooks Tomblin)

records.notes: Dealer blog; Enduro21 (2023) notes a TBI version was announced after the TPI one.

records.statement: The TBI ECU has no closed-loop fuel correction for engine changes, so head work, porting or a pipe can make it run lean; tuners say any pipe or head change needs a matching remap.

source.name: Vital MX - 2023 KTM 125SX deep dive: EFI, tune, mods

records.notes: JBoneMotorworks (2022) and lumpy790 (2024) on Vital MX; consistent with Twisted Development offering pipe-specific maps.

records.statement: Yamaha lists the YZ250 at 66.4 x 72 mm, 249 cc, compression ratio 8.9 to 10.6:1, with a Keihin PWK38S carburetor with power jet and a 5-speed gearbox.

values.carburetor: Keihin PWK38S w/ power jet + TPS

source.name: Yamaha Motor USA - 2024 YZ250 50th Anniversary specifications

records.notes: Yamaha does not say how the two compression figures are measured. MXA quotes the YZ250 as 8.9:1 with a 21.5 cc head, so the low figure is the one tuners quote.

records.statement: Yamaha lists the 2022-on YZ125 at 54 x 54.5 mm, 125 cc, compression ratio 8.2 to 10.1:1, with a Keihin PWK38S carburetor with power jet and TPS and a 6-speed gearbox.

values.carburetor: Keihin PWK38S w/ power jet + TPS

source.name: Yamaha Motor USA - 2023 YZ125 specifications

records.topic: 2022 YZ125 redesign - combustion chamber and compression
records.statement: The 2022 YZ125 chamber is 1.6 mm taller with 2.4% more volume, dropping compression from 8.57 to 8.20:1.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2022 Yamaha YZ125

records.notes: Yamaha figures as reported by MXA.

records.statement: The 2022 YZ125 got a larger exhaust port and bigger, lower, wider transfer ports; the cylinder base was enlarged and the front studs moved 3 mm forward to fit them. The exhaust duct is shorter and the intake port larger.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2022 Yamaha YZ125

records.notes: Enduro21 (Yamaha Europe) adds 'shorter exhaust port'. No port heights or timings published.

records.statement: The 2022 YZ125 rod is 8 mm longer, crankcase 8 mm taller at the cylinder joint, crank inertia up 2.7% and flywheel inertia up 21%.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2022 Yamaha YZ125

records.notes: Absolute rod length not published in sources found.

records.topic: 2022 YZ125 redesign - power valve, intake and exhaust
records.statement: Yamaha changed YPVS shape, maximum lift and opening/closing timing for 2022, fitted a V-Force reed block and a 15% lower-resistance intake, narrowed the pipe belly and shortened the silencer about 50 mm (to 17 in).

source.name: Enduro21 - First look: Yamaha's new 2022 YZ range (YZ125)

records.notes: Combined from Enduro21 (Yamaha Europe release) and MXA.

records.statement: From 2022 the YZ125 uses a Keihin PWK38S with a solenoid power jet that adds fuel between 5,000 and 9,500 rpm above half throttle, replacing the 38 mm Mikuni TMX.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2022 Yamaha YZ125

records.statement: The 2022-on YZ125 CDI uses throttle position plus rpm (a 3D map) to set ignition timing.

source.name: Cycle News - 2022 Yamaha YZ125 review

records.notes: Map values not published.

records.statement: The YZ250 power valve is driven by a crank-gear centrifugal governor and has three pieces: a center valve that opens in the first half of control-rod rotation and two side valves that open in the second half, held by torsion springs that default it closed.

source.name: US Patent 9,797,275 B1 - Motorcycle engine power valve control upgrade kit (Timothy B. King)

records.notes: Description from US patent 9,797,275 (aftermarket inventor describing the stock 1999-on design). The patent attributes the YZ250's mid-rpm 'hit' to the center valve reaching its stop, where friction and spring force cause hesitation then surge.

records.statement: Yamaha fits carbon-fibre reed petals to the YZ250.

source.name: Yamaha Motor USA - 2024 YZ250 50th Anniversary features

records.statement: MXA describes the YZ250 as largely unchanged since 2006, with the last notable update in 2022 being bodywork, seat and subframe; it remains carbureted with a mechanical power valve and kick start.

source.name: Motocross Action - Video: 2025 Yamaha YZ250 two-stroke test

records.notes: MXA 2020 race test notes a 2011 change: silencer lengthened 75 mm and compression revised so the bike runs a wider range of US/European fuels.

records.statement: Owners measure the stock YZ250 head at about 21.5 cc with squish around 0.072-0.075 in (1.8-1.9 mm); heads vary by code: 5UP 21.0 cc, 5CU 22.0 cc, 5WM 21.5 cc, YZ250X head 23.5 cc.

source.name: Vital MX - 2013 YZ250 (2-stroke) head questions

records.notes: Forum measurements (cwtoyota, slipdog, digger). MXA independently quotes 21.5 cc for the YZ250 and 23.6 cc for the YZ250X.

records.statement: Yamaha softened the YZ250X by raising head volume from 21.5 to 23.6 cc (compression 8.9 to 7.9:1), raising the exhaust port 0.5 mm with a matching valve shape, retarding the CDI in the mid-to-high range, and setting the governor spring/preload to open the valve sooner; the pipe is 35 mm narrower.

source.name: Motocross Action - Ask the MXperts: the X factor versus the non-X factor

records.notes: Yamaha changes as reported by MXA. Result: milder hit, tractable to 6,500 rpm, dip at 7,000 picking up at 7,400, same peak around 8,800 rpm, more over-rev. A real-world example of how head volume, port height, ignition and PV timing move a two-stroke's power.

records.statement: MXA measured the 2023 300SX at 55.0 hp at 8,500 rpm in map 2 and 54.19 hp in map 1; about 27 hp at 5,000, 34 at 6,000, 39 at 6,500, 45 at 7,000 and just over 50 at 7,500 rpm.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2023 KTM 300SX

records.notes: Dyno type not stated (MXA). Stock bike, premix. Maps identical until 6,700 rpm.

records.statement: Dirt Rider's Dynojet 250i measured the 2023 300 SX at 48.8 hp at 8,100 rpm and 32.2 lb-ft at 7,500 rpm.

source.name: Dirt Rider - How much power does the 2023 KTM 300 SX make? (Andrew Oldar)

records.notes: Dynojet 250i, rear wheel. Map not stated. Not comparable with MXA's dyno.

records.statement: Dirt Rider's Dynojet 250i measured the 2025 300 SX at 49.1 hp and 32.3 lb-ft at the rear wheel.

source.name: Dirt Rider - How much power does the 2025 KTM 300 SX make? (Andrew Oldar)

records.notes: Dynojet 250i; rpm and map not stated. 5.7 lb-ft more than the 2025 350 SX-F on the same dyno.

records.statement: MXA measured the 2024 250SX at about 52.1 hp at 8,600 rpm and the 300SX at about 55 hp at 8,500 rpm.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2024 KTM 250/300SX

records.notes: Dyno type not stated.

records.statement: MXA's dyno showed the 2023 Husqvarna TC250 TBI peaking at 52.12 hp at 8,600 rpm.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2023 KTM 300SX

records.notes: Quoted for comparison in MXA's 2023 300SX test; dyno type not stated.

records.statement: Dirt Rider's Dynojet 250i measured the 2025 TC 250 Heritage at 43.0 hp and 29.6 lb-ft.

source.name: Dirt Rider - How much power does the 2025 Husqvarna TC 250 Heritage make? (Andrew Oldar)

records.notes: Dynojet 250i; rpm and map not stated.

records.statement: Dirt Rider's Dynojet 250i measured the TBI 125 SX at 30.9 hp at 10,800 rpm and 15.3 lb-ft at 10,700 rpm.

source.name: Dirt Rider - KTM 125 SX dyno test (Andrew Oldar)

records.notes: Published Sept 2023 under a '2023' URL; likely the 2024 model. Spec table lists a 44 mm throttle body, conflicting with KTM's 39 mm.

records.statement: MXA measured the 2024 TBI 125SX at 37.2 hp at 11,200 rpm vs 38.2 hp at 11,400 rpm for the 2022 carbureted bike; the curves match to about 10,800 rpm, then the TBI bike falls off, and it is slightly slower off the bottom.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2024 KTM 125SX

records.notes: Dyno type not stated. MXA says port timing and compression were unchanged 2022 to 2024.

source.name: Dirt Bike - 125 2-strokes on the dyno (Pro Circuit dyno)

records.notes: Pro Circuit dyno (Dynojet per Dirt Bike's earlier dyno articles). Stock status not stated; model years assumed 2024 (article Feb 2024).

records.statement: MXA measured carbureted 2022 125s: KTM 125SX 38.5 hp, GasGas MC125 37.8, Husqvarna TC125 37.7 (all at 11,200 rpm) and YZ125 35.9 hp at 11,600 rpm.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2022 125 two-stroke shootout

records.notes: Dyno type not stated.

records.statement: MXA measured the 2022 YZ125 at 34.44 hp at 11,300 rpm vs 33.38 hp for the 2021; the 2022 is up to 1.5 hp down at 6,500 rpm, crosses near 7,500 and leads from 10,000 rpm to peak.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2022 Yamaha YZ125

records.notes: Same dyno, same day; type not stated. Reference engines in the same article: KTM 125SX 37.52 hp, Pro Circuit replica 38.32 hp.

records.statement: MXA measured the 2021 YZ125 at 33.53 hp and the KTM 125SX at 37.50 hp, both peaking at 11,500 rpm; the YZ makes more below 7,800 rpm and the KTM leads by 2.5 hp from 7,900 to peak.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2021 Yamaha YZ125

records.notes: Same day; dyno type not stated.

records.statement: MXA measured the 2020 YZ125 at 34.50 hp and KTM 125SX at 37.50 hp (11,200 rpm); torque 16.29 lb-ft @ 11,000 vs 17.69 @ 11,100. The YZ made more below 8,000 rpm, the KTM was up about 3 hp at 11,000.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2020 KTM 125SX vs 2020 Yamaha YZ125 unshootout

records.notes: Article prints two YZ peaks; dyno type not stated; both bikes on the same 38 mm Mikuni TMX.

records.statement: MXA measured the 2023 YZ125 at 35.64 hp, revving to about 11,700 rpm, about 1.5 hp behind the KTM/Husky and almost 3 hp behind the GasGas MC125.

source.name: Motocross Action - Test update 2023 Yamaha YZ125

records.notes: Dyno type not stated.

records.statement: MXA's stock YZ250 made 46.85 hp at 8,700 rpm and 30.33 lb-ft at 7,600, holding over 44 hp from 7,900 to 9,100 rpm: 21.81 hp at 5,000, 30.95 at 6,000, 39.61 at 7,000, 44.32 at 8,000, 45.92 at 9,000.

source.name: Motocross Action - Searching for the ultimate YZ250 two-stroke pipe (2013)

records.notes: 2013 model on 91-octane pump gas with Yamalube R; dyno model not stated. Engine is largely unchanged through 2026 per MXA, so this is the best published curve shape for the current engine, but not a 2020-2026 measurement.

records.statement: VHM Racing measured a stock 2026 YZ250 at 43.7 hp and 31.3 lb-ft; with a higher-compression head, CDI change and HGS exhaust it made 47.5 hp and 34.4 lb-ft (+3.8 hp, +3.1 lb-ft).

source.name: Vital MX - 2026 Beta 250 RX vs 2026 Yamaha YZ250 dyno tests (VHM Racing data posted by Tokyo_Tiddler)

records.notes: Shop dyno data posted second-hand on Vital MX; dyno brand, rpm, fuel not stated. A 2026 Beta 250 RX on the same dyno (other day) made 46.2 hp stock.

records.statement: Dick's Racing's 300 conversion (KTM PowerParts kit, 1 mm higher port timing, head machined 1 mm, 36 mm Keihin bored to 39 mm, Scalvini pipe) made 53.2 hp, about 4.2 hp more than the stock 250SX; it was never within 2 hp of it anywhere.

source.name: Motocross Action - We ride Dick's Racing's massaged KTM 300SX

records.notes: Carbureted 2021 base bike; dyno type not stated.

records.statement: Testers describe smooth, linear roll-on with no bog, a strong lug-able midrange (2nd and 3rd in turns) and power that keeps building to about 8,500 rpm, but an abrupt rev limiter, most intrusive in the air or with the clutch pulled.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2023 KTM 300SX

records.notes: Paraphrased tester impressions (MXA 2023 and 2024).

records.statement: The 250SX TBI is smooth and connected off the bottom, needs more shifting than the 300 in the midrange and revs through the gears quicker, but runs flat near the top and hits the limiter early.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2024 KTM 250/300SX

records.statement: Dirt Bike found the TBI TC250 stronger down low than any 250 two-stroke they had tested, with a big surge at peak but little excitement on top; the aggressive map is worth more than 1 hp in parts of the curve. White map feels close to a four-stroke.

values.map_gain: >1 hp in parts of curve (Pro Circuit dyno)

source.name: Dirt Bike - Riding the 2023 Husky TC250 2-stroke

records.notes: MotoOnline describes the same white/green map character.

records.statement: The TBI 125SX rolls on smoother with less on/off hit and less clutch work than the 2022 carbureted bike, is fast in the middle and pulls hard on top but has an abrupt limiter; testers shift early.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2024 KTM 125SX

records.notes: Dirt Bike 2024 testers said the Austrian TBI 125s feel more enduro-like and respond less to clutch work.

records.statement: Since 2022 the YZ125 is weaker off the bottom and slower to come on the pipe than the 2021, but stronger from about 7,500 rpm to its 11,300 rpm peak; pros liked it, beginners struggled and riders clutch more out of turns.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2022 Yamaha YZ125

records.notes: Dirt Bike 2024 riders still rated the YZ125 strongest in the midrange despite the dyno, crediting low flywheel effect.

records.statement: Pre-2022 YZ125s pulled harder than the KTM 125SX below about 7,800-8,000 rpm and were easier to keep on the pipe; above 8,000 the KTM was described as night-and-day faster.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2020 KTM 125SX vs 2020 Yamaha YZ125 unshootout

records.statement: In MXA's 2020 test the YZ250 made its best power higher in the rpm and did not like being lugged, needing clutch out of corners, while the KTM/Husky 250s were better low-to-mid; the YZ was slower but easier to ride.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2020 Yamaha YZ250

records.notes: Conflicts with MXA's 2015/2016 shootout which called the YZ250 broad with enough low-end torque; see conflicts.

records.statement: On the stock pipe, MXA riders felt a stutter when the YZ250 power valve opens and a flat spot from about 7,000 to 8,500 rpm.

source.name: Motocross Action - Searching for the ultimate YZ250 two-stroke pipe (2013)

records.notes: Consistent with the governor 'hitch' described in US patent 9,797,275 and the community governor mods.

records.statement: The DR.D NS2 pipe on a stock YZ250 made 47.44 hp @ 7,900 and 32.17 lb-ft @ 7,500 versus stock 46.85 hp; change by rpm: 5000 -1.05, 6000 +0.38, 7000 +1.94, 8000 +3.02, 9000 -3.04 hp. Strongest midrange, pulls very hard in the middle but does not want to rev; flat above ~8,000.

source.name: Motocross Action - Searching for the ultimate YZ250 two-stroke pipe (2013)

records.notes: MXA 2013 test, same dyno, same day, 91 pump gas, stock silencer. Engine design carries through 2026 but pipe part numbers may differ for current frames.

records.topic: pipe - Pro Circuit Works on YZ250
records.statement: The Pro Circuit Works pipe on a stock YZ250 made 49.33 hp @ 8,600 and 31.67 lb-ft @ 7,800 versus stock 46.85 hp; change by rpm: 5000 -0.38, 6000 -0.46, 7000 +0.06, 8000 +3.46, 9000 -0.21 hp. Average or worse below ~7,600, best above: a mid-and-up pipe.

source.name: Motocross Action - Searching for the ultimate YZ250 two-stroke pipe (2013)

records.notes: MXA 2013 test, same dyno, same day, 91 pump gas, stock silencer. Engine design carries through 2026 but pipe part numbers may differ for current frames.

records.statement: The FMF Fatty pipe on a stock YZ250 made 47.71 hp @ 8,700 and 31.90 lb-ft @ 7,800 versus stock 46.85 hp; change by rpm: 5000 -0.56, 6000 -0.26, 7000 +0.72, 8000 +3.01, 9000 -0.92 hp. Most balanced; riders wanted more top.

source.name: Motocross Action - Searching for the ultimate YZ250 two-stroke pipe (2013)

records.notes: MXA 2013 test, same dyno, same day, 91 pump gas, stock silencer. Engine design carries through 2026 but pipe part numbers may differ for current frames.

records.statement: A Pro Circuit Works pipe and 304 silencer took the 2022 YZ125 from 34.4 hp at 11,500 to 35.8 hp at 11,600 rpm; no change below 9,500 rpm, then faster build, broader top and more over-rev.

source.name: Motocross Action - Team tested Pro Circuit 2022 YZ125 pipe and silencer

records.notes: Jetting used: main 162, pilot 72, clip up, air screw 3.5 out. Pre-2022 YZ125 pipes do not fit the 2022 engine.

records.statement: MXA says aftermarket pipes add about 2 hp to the YZ125; porting works best combined with raised compression, which means milling the cylinder base (lowering all ports) and re-chambering the head, and usually race gas. Pro Circuit's standard pipe favors top end, its RV pipe low-mid.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2021 Yamaha YZ125

records.notes: Reeds: Boyesen Rad Valve for mid-to-top, Moto Tassinari VForce4 to broaden the midrange. GYTR flywheel weights fill the powerband and extend top end.

records.topic: YZ250 DR.D pipe and Boyesen RAD valve
records.statement: MXA's 2015 YZ250 build with a DR.D pipe, Boyesen RAD power-valve cover and Power X-Wing gained bottom-end and midrange pull, letting the rider carry 3rd gear and lug corners without stalling.

source.name: Motocross Action - Two-stroke files: we built a full-race Yamaha YZ250 (2015)

records.notes: No dyno numbers given.

records.statement: Owners re-time the YZ250 governor by swapping two 1.0 mm thrust washers for 0.8 mm YZ250X washers and removing one, cutting spring preload by about 1.4 mm so the valve opens earlier; it fills the off-idle dip but needs a leaner power jet (#35 reported).

records.notes: Spring data quoted in thread: stock YZ spring 0.640 in installed, ~18 lb preload, 40 lb at full compression; YZ250X spring 0.672 in, 19-20 lb preload, 52-53 lb.

records.notes: Seller claim; no rate or dyno data.

records.topic: TSP high-compression head and PV cover (TBI)
records.statement: Two Stroke Performance sells a two-piece head with tighter-than-stock squish in medium (91 octane, sea level), high, and very-high (above 4,900 ft) compression, plus a larger power-valve cover claimed to add pull from 3,000 to 5,000 rpm.

source.name: Slavens Racing blog - TSP parts for TBI KTM two-strokes (Brooks Tomblin)

records.notes: Claims without published dyno data.

records.statement: Derek Harris ranks the pipe as the single most important part, then scavenging (keeping the charge in the cylinder), then matching pipe to ignition curve and compression; carburetor and case work matter less.

source.name: Vital MX - Hierarchy of two-stroke hop-ups (Derek Harris reply)

records.notes: Forum post by a known engine builder; figures are his estimates.

records.statement: A port open for a fixed number of crank degrees is open for less time as rpm rises: time = degrees / (6 x rpm). A 190-degree exhaust port is open 3.7 ms at 8,600 rpm but 7.9 ms at 4,000 rpm, which is why a tall port suits high rpm and wastes charge at low rpm.

source.name: Cycle World - Tuned exhaust for the two-stroke (Gordon H. Jennings)

records.notes: t = theta/(6N): 190/(6*8600) = 0.00368 s; 190/(6*4000) = 0.00792 s. Formula from Jennings 1964. 190 deg is an illustrative duration, not a measured figure for any bike here.

records.statement: Jennings' handbook sizes ports by time-area (port area x open time per cc of swept volume): about 0.00014-0.00015 s-cm2/cm3 for exhaust, 0.00008-0.00010 for transfers and 0.00014-0.00016 for piston-port intake. Motocross engines run less exhaust and more transfer time-area than road racers for smoother power.

source.name: Ring Ding Riders blog - Analysis of the port timing section from Jennings' Two-Stroke Tuner's Handbook

records.notes: Second-hand summary of Gordon Jennings, Two-Stroke Tuner's Handbook (1973). Specific time-area = mean port area x (degrees/(6N)) / swept volume.

records.topic: principle - raise vs widen the exhaust port
records.statement: Raising the exhaust port opens it earlier, adding duration and time-area: peak power moves up the rpm range but the band narrows and bottom end is lost. Widening adds area without adding duration, so it gains top end while keeping the band broader.

source.name: Ring Ding Riders blog - Analysis of the port timing section from Jennings' Two-Stroke Tuner's Handbook

records.notes: Jennings via summary; dt125r tuner thread (Calum) also notes raising the barrel lowers trapped compression and changes every port's timing, so it needs head and ignition rework. Yamaha's YZ250X (+0.5 mm exhaust plus lower compression) gains over-rev and loses hit.

records.statement: Blowdown is the crank angle between the exhaust opening and the transfers opening; it lets cylinder pressure fall before fresh charge enters. Because port timings are symmetric about BDC, exhaust duration = transfer duration + 2 x blowdown.

values.example: exhaust 90 deg ATDC, transfers 115 deg ATDC = 25 deg blowdown

source.name: Marty's Garage - Two-stroke port duration reference

records.notes: Identity follows from symmetric piston-port timing. Marty's Garage table (moped-oriented) suggests about 19 deg blowdown at 6,000 rpm rising to 32 deg at 10,000; KDX200 example: exhaust 188, transfers 126, blowdown 32 deg. Treat the rpm table as rough guidance, not MX data.

records.topic: principle - what a power valve does
records.statement: A fixed exhaust port height only works over a narrow rpm range. The power valve lowers the effective port top at low rpm (shorter duration, more trapped compression, pipe working better) and raises it at high rpm (more duration and time-area), widening the usable band.

source.name: Wikipedia - Two-stroke power valve system

records.notes: Yamaha's SAE paper 810922 (1981) says varying exhaust timing with speed raised output by improving delivery ratio and trapping efficiency. Historical YPVS example (RD350 street bike): about 180 deg closed below 6,000 rpm to 200 deg fully open by 8,000 rpm (rd350lc.net, citing the service manual).

records.topic: principle - power valve opening rpm and feel
records.statement: Opening the valve earlier smooths the hit and fills the low-mid dip but can lose some punch; opening it later or snapping it open faster makes a harder, more aggressive hit and more top end.

source.name: Motocross Action - Ask the MXperts: fine-tuning the KTM 250SX two-stroke

records.notes: Supported by KTM spring/preload guidance (MXA, ADB), YZ250X governor setting (MXA) and YZ250 governor mods (Vital).

records.statement: The pipe's diverging cone sends a suction wave back that pulls exhaust out and draws fresh charge through the transfers; the converging (baffle) cone then sends a pressure wave that pushes escaping charge back in before the port closes. Both waves only arrive at the right time in a band of rpm.

source.name: Cycle World - Tuned exhaust for the two-stroke (Gordon H. Jennings)

records.notes: Gordon Jennings, Cycle World 1964.

records.statement: Wave travel time is fixed by length and gas temperature, so the tuned rpm moves inversely with pipe length: shortening the tuned length about 4.4% moves the tuned rpm from 8,600 to about 9,000 rpm.

source.name: BAK MX engineering calculation

records.notes: L = Vs x t / 2 with t = theta/(6N) (Jennings 1964), so L is proportional to 1/N at fixed wave speed and crank angle: 8,600/9,000 = 0.956, i.e. 4.4% shorter.

records.statement: Hotter exhaust gas raises wave speed, so the same pipe tunes to a higher rpm: going from about 500 to 600 deg C raises wave speed about 6%, shifting the tuned rpm roughly 6% higher. Leaner jetting, retarded ignition and smaller stingers run the pipe hotter.

source.name: Moped Army wiki - Expansion chamber

records.notes: Speed of sound proportional to sqrt(T_abs): sqrt(873/773) = 1.063. Moped Army wiki lists heat wrap, smaller stinger and later ignition as ways to raise temperature and water injection as lowering it.

records.statement: Header holds wave energy during blowdown; the diffuser (about 6-12 degrees) makes the suction wave; the belly diameter trades scavenging suction against port-plugging; the baffle cone makes the plugging wave; the stinger's inside diameter sets chamber pressure. Gentler cones broaden the band but lower the peak.

source.name: Moped Army wiki - Expansion chamber

records.notes: Matches MXA's YZ250 pipe test: different shapes on the same engine moved gains between 7,000 and 9,000 rpm by up to 3 hp either way.

records.statement: Squish effectiveness falls off above about 1.2-1.25 mm; builders target roughly 0.8-1.0 mm on small bores, with the band angle about 1 degree steeper than the piston crown. Tighter squish and higher compression need more octane.

source.name: KDXRider.net - Modifying heads for proper squish height, squish area/velocity and dome cc (Chuck78)

records.notes: Forum author Chuck78 (KDXRider). VHM uses 0.9 mm on the KTM 125 and 1.0 mm on the YZ125, but 1.6 mm (250) and 1.9 mm (300) on larger bores.

records.statement: On the VHM 250 TBI head, going from the 22.6 cc to the 21.4 cc insert raises full-stroke compression by roughly 0.6 of a ratio point, which is why the smaller insert calls for 105 RON fuel.

source.name: BAK MX engineering calculation

records.notes: CR = (249 + Vc)/Vc: (249+21.4)/21.4 = 12.64; (249+22.6)/22.6 = 12.02. Assumes VHM insert volume is the whole clearance volume, which it may not be (squish gap and gasket not included), so absolute ratios are indicative only. Trapped (exhaust-closed) compression is much lower and needs port height, which is unpublished.

records.statement: The 250s are undersquare (66.4/72 = 0.92), the 300 is square (1.00) and the 125s are near square (0.99). At their measured peaks, all run about 20.4-20.9 m/s mean piston speed: 250SX 20.6 m/s at 8,600, YZ250 20.9 at 8,700, 300SX 20.4 at 8,500, KTM 125 20.3 at 11,200, YZ125 20.5 at 11,300 rpm.

source.name: BAK MX engineering calculation

records.notes: Mean piston speed = 2 x stroke(mm) x rpm / 60000. Peak rpm from MXA dynos (2024 250SX, 2013 YZ250, 2023 300SX, 2021 KTM 125SX, 2022 YZ125). Similar piston speeds at peak suggest both brands tune ports/pipes to similar gas-flow limits; the 125s peak higher purely because of their shorter stroke.

records.statement: With about 150 rpm per turn and six turns of range, the KTM mechanical power-valve preload screw can move the opening point by roughly 900 rpm in total.

source.name: BAK MX engineering calculation

records.notes: 6 turns x 150 rpm/turn = 900 rpm (MXA/ADB inputs). Assumes the 150 rpm/turn rate is linear across the whole range, which no source confirms.

records.statement: More flywheel inertia smooths delivery and helps traction but slows how fast the engine revs; Yamaha added 21% flywheel inertia to the 2022 YZ125 to match its higher output, and tuners use GYTR flywheel weights to fill the powerband.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2021 Yamaha YZ125

records.notes: Dirt Bike credits the YZ125's quick-revving midrange feel to low flywheel effect.

records.topic: principle - ignition timing and power valve on feel (Yamaha example)
records.statement: Yamaha's own softening recipe for the YZ250X combines mid-to-high rpm ignition retard, earlier power-valve opening and lower compression; the result is a milder hit and broader pull with the same peak, showing how these three levers interact.

source.name: Motocross Action - Ask the MXperts: the X factor versus the non-X factor

records.notes: Interpretation of Yamaha's documented changes; see 2t record on YZ250 vs YZ250X.
